site.name: HOMAYOUN SHEIKHI
site.role: Media Executive · Filmmaker · Creative Producer · Screenwriter
site.heroText: More than 25 years of professional experience across television, film, radio and digital media — combining creative leadership, production management and storytelling.

about.intro: A media professional working across creative development, production, storytelling and original audiovisual content.
about.heading: Media leadership with a storyteller's perspective.
about.text: My work brings together creative development, production management and storytelling — from large-scale television programming to independent radio, documentary and digital projects.
about.closing: I have worked across the full life cycle of media projects: concept development, editorial direction, writing, production planning, team leadership, delivery and audience-facing presentation.

bring.text: Writing, narration and voice performance shaped around clarity, presence and audience connection.

projects.title: Hope Dead End
projects.label: Short Film
projects.text: A man arrives at a hospital with his wife’s medical records showing liver failure. The social worker informs him that a liver transplant has been preliminarily approved — provided his wife is hospitalised for monitoring.

projects.title: Ab o Khak (Territory / Homeland)
projects.label: Feature Film
projects.text: After the body of an Iraqi soldier from the Iran–Iraq war (1980–1988) is discovered on the Arvand River shoreline, three families from Iran, Iraq and the UK — from three different decades — meet in strange circumstances.

projects.title: Giti to ra pasandid (The World Likes You)
projects.label: Documentary
projects.text: A report on the 2013 Asian Futsal Championship in Nagoya, focusing on the Iranian team Giti Pasand, which won second place.

projects.title: ABADAN Refinery
projects.label: Industrial Documentary
projects.text: An introduction to Iran’s most famous oil refinery.

projects.title: DA (Mother)
projects.label: Documentary
projects.text: Based on the best-selling book “One Woman’s War”, this film tells the story of Seyyedeh Zahra Hosseini, a 17-year-old girl during the Iran–Iraq war in 1980 who defended her city of Khorramshahr. It offers both an epic account of resistance and a critical view of war’s destructive effects.
